A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPS research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original mathematics and Countdown experiments, prediction-quality measurements, ablations, and test-time allocation results, including extensive appendix evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds mixed mathematics/code training, embedding sensitivity, and HH-RLHF results in Tables 5–7.

M1.justification: Appendix E.13 adds an RLHF adaptation that predicts mean continuous reward and uses quantile-threshold selection. This supplements the reward-variance prediction variant already present in E.5. The main GPS architecture, ELBO, and difficulty/diversity selection procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 substantially broadens coverage beyond the existing mathematics, Countdown, and general-reasoning evaluations. E.11 adds joint DeepScaler/Prime Code training and CodeContests/Codeforces evaluation; E.13 adds HH-RLHF, extending evaluation beyond reasoning tasks.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain Uniform, PCL, GRESO, MoPPS, and DS, with Default and Random retained for test-time allocation. The added experiments reuse Uniform; no new competing selection method is evaluated. Embedding substitutions are sensitivity variants.

E3.justification: The added studies introduce Qwen3-1.7B-Base configurations, Avg@4 coding evaluation, and controlled embedding substitutions on Countdown (E.11–E.13). Previously specified experimental settings remain unchanged. The new RLHF evaluation protocol is only briefly documented.

E4.justification: E.12 and Table 6 newly test sensitivity to the embedding model by comparing WordLlama, all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and bge-large-en-v1.5 on Countdown. Existing component ablations, hyperparameter studies, training-dynamics analyses, and PRIME experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same correlation p-values and significance annotations without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or testing procedures. Table 7's new correlation range is not identified as an uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Tables 5–7 substantially extend the reported findings while existing results remain unchanged. In the new mixed-domain setting, GPS versus Uniform averages are 34.0 versus 31.5 for mathematics and 26.5 versus 24.3 for coding. New embedding variants score 67.9 and 67.7. The RLHF study reports 1.24× speedup and performance of 18.1 versus 17.4, although that performance metric is unspecified.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, its Appendix C proof, the generative-model derivation, and the mathematical selection/allocation definitions are retained. Added explanatory prose does not introduce a new theorem, assumption, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three central contributions and headline claims: up to 2.0× training acceleration, 69% fewer rollouts, 36.4% inference savings, and 3.2% fixed-budget improvement. New appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.3 newly states that predictive correlation diminishes on semantically distant tasks and suggests multi-domain co-training. E.13 explicitly characterizes RLHF selection as heuristic, while E.14 adds discussion of possible offline and interactive applications.

D1.justification: V2 adds a GPS code-repository link in the abstract and identifies the alternative embedding implementations in E.12. Existing Appendix D implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware disclosures are essentially unchanged; detailed reproduction instructions for the new RLHF experiment remain limited.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds citations concerning predictive sampling, batch selection, and policy optimization, including Mao et al. (2026) and Zou et al. (2025). E.14 extends the cited context to offline RL and interactive environments. The central positioning against prompt-specific predictors remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. V2 adds targeted explanations, an Impact Statement, and Appendix E.11–E.14, alongside limited citation, header, and cross-reference editing.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column format to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and repositioning text, equations, the algorithm, and figures. Tables 5–7 are added. Existing Figures 1–13 retain their graphical content despite relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: The mixed-domain evaluation broadens empirical support, and the embedding sensitivity study tests flexibility previously asserted largely in discussion. The code link and explicit domain-transfer qualification improve transparency. These are useful incremental gains, tempered by incomplete reporting of the new RLHF experiment, particularly its undefined performance metric and sparse evaluation details.
